columns.comment: Calendar month of the payment as its first day (DATE): September 2026 = DATE'2026-09-01' (the month-end snapshot as of 30-Sep-2026). This view is monthly; point-in-time measures grouped by a longer period (quarter, half, fiscal year) return its last month. The latest month is Sep 2026.
columns.name: Month

columns.comment: Japanese fiscal year label of the payment, April to March: FY2026 = Apr 2026 - Mar 2027, FY2025 = Apr 2025 - Mar 2026. "This year" / YTD = FY2026 to 30-Sep-2026; year-on-year compares the same months of FY2025.
columns.name: Fiscal Year

columns.comment: Japanese fiscal quarter label, e.g. FY2026-Q2: Q1 = Apr-Jun, Q2 = Jul-Sep, Q3 = Oct-Dec, Q4 = Jan-Mar (FY2026-Q4 = Jan-Mar 2027). The latest quarter is FY2026-Q2 (Jul-Sep 2026).
columns.name: Fiscal Quarter

columns.comment: Japanese fiscal half label, e.g. FY2026-H1: H1 = Apr-Sep, H2 = Oct-Mar. H1 FY2026 (Apr-Sep 2026) closed on 30-Sep-2026; compare with FY2025-H1 for year-on-year.
columns.name: Fiscal Half

columns.comment: Always true here: this view is monthly, every row is a month-end snapshot or a whole-month total (kept so the same filter works in daily and monthly views).
columns.name: Is Month End

columns.comment: True for September 2026, the latest (as-of) month - use it for "today", "current", "latest" or "right now" questions on balances and other point-in-time measures.
columns.name: Is Latest Month

columns.comment: Client group = the global parent group, as its short brand (e.g. Kinokawa Precision, Hayashi Marine Logistics, Sunda Energi Nusantara). "Client" or "group" without qualification means this level. Match names with LIKE '%Kinokawa%'. About 380 groups.
columns.name: Client Group

columns.comment: Legal entity (golden client) with its location, e.g. Kinokawa Precision (Singapore) Pte Ltd - "entity" or "subsidiary" means this level. About 2,500 entities; match with LIKE '%Kinokawa%Singapore%'.
columns.name: Client

columns.comment: Client segment: Japanese Corporate, Non-Japanese Large Corporate, Financial Institution, Sponsor & Structured Finance or Public Sector.
columns.name: Segment

columns.comment: Relationship tier - Strategic, Core or Transactional. "Strategic clients" means Relationship Tier = Strategic.
columns.name: Relationship Tier

columns.comment: True for APAC subsidiaries of Japanese groups (segment Japanese Corporate) - "Japanese corporates", "JC" or "Japanese clients" means true.
columns.name: Is Japanese Corporate

columns.comment: Industry sector of the APAC taxonomy (e.g. Technology, Materials, Energy, Industrials); see Subsector.
columns.name: Industry

columns.comment: Industry subsector within the sector (e.g. Semiconductors, Automotive Parts, Coal Mining, Shipping).
columns.name: Subsector

columns.comment: Coverage office of the paying / receiving client (ISO-2). For payments it equals Booking Country (the client account's booking location) - prefer Booking Country.
columns.name: Coverage Office

columns.comment: Primary relationship manager (fictional name) at the row's month-end: the CRM primary-RM assignment, else the group account-plan owner; null = no RM coverage.
columns.name: Primary RM

columns.comment: Office (APAC booking location, ISO-2) where the primary RM sits - "RMs in Singapore / Hong Kong" means this (most RMs also cover clients booked in other countries, so it differs from Coverage Office).
columns.name: Primary RM Office

columns.comment: Internal rating grade 1-10 in force at the row's month-end (1 best, 10 default; 7 and worse is sub-investment watch territory); null = not rated (no credit relationship).
columns.name: Rating Grade

columns.comment: IFRS 9 stage at the row's month-end: 1 performing, 2 significant increase in credit risk, 3 credit-impaired / default; null = not rated.
columns.name: IFRS 9 Stage

columns.comment: True when the client is on the credit watchlist at the row's month-end ("not on the watchlist" = false).
columns.name: Watchlist

columns.comment: KYC / AML risk rating Low, Medium or High at the row's month-end (latest completed review); null = no KYC record.
columns.name: KYC Risk Rating

columns.comment: Final early-warning band at the row's month-end: Green (score < 40), Amber (40-69) or Red (>= 70), after overrides; null = not scored (no credit relationship, or before Apr-2025).
columns.name: EWS Band

columns.comment: APAC booking location of the client account the payment is booked to (ISO-2: SG, HK, CN, TH, ID, IN, AU, VN, MY, KR, TW, PH, NZ). "Country" in payment questions means this unless the user says counterparty country.
columns.name: Booking Country

columns.comment: Channel / rail of the payment: SWIFT MT, ISO 20022, Host-to-Host, Payments API, Portal (e-banking), RTGS or FAST. Digital channels = Portal, Payments API, Host-to-Host.
columns.name: Channel

columns.comment: Inbound (the client receives money) or Outbound (the client pays).
columns.name: Direction

columns.comment: Purpose of the payment: Supplier, Payroll, Tax, Intercompany, Loan Service (debt service to a lender), Dividend or Trade Settlement.
columns.name: Payment Purpose

columns.comment: ISO 4217 currency of the client account the payment is booked to (amounts are reported in USD).
columns.name: Currency

columns.comment: True for cross-border payments (payer and payee in different countries, as flagged by the payments hub).
columns.name: Is Cross-Border

columns.comment: Money-flow corridor payer country->payee country, e.g. CN->VN = money paid from China to Vietnam (Kinokawa's China entity paying Vietnam). Domestic payments show the same country twice (SG->SG).
columns.name: Corridor

columns.comment: Country of the counterparty (beneficiary of an outbound payment, remitter of an inbound one), ISO-2.
columns.name: Counterparty Country

columns.comment: Where the counterparty banks: SMBC (on-us), Other Bank (a competitor bank - wallet leakage) or Intercompany (a transfer within the client group).
columns.name: Counterparty Bank Type

columns.comment: Counterparty bank name: SMBC, Intercompany or a fictional competitor (e.g. Nordlys Bank, Garuda Commercial Bank, Meridian Pacific Bank).
columns.name: Counterparty Bank

columns.comment: Why a payment needed manual repair: FX cover missing, Invalid BIC, Missing beneficiary, Sanctions hold, Format error or Duplicate instruction; null for straight-through (STP) payments.
columns.name: Repair Reason

columns.comment: Value of the selected payments in USD (a flow - adds up over months).
columns.name: Payment Volume USD

columns.comment: Number of payment messages (one per payment; the June-2026 replay duplicates are removed).
columns.name: Payments

columns.comment: Average payment size in USD = volume / number of payments.
columns.name: Average Ticket USD

columns.comment: Share of payments processed straight through without manual repair (fraction; 0.92 = 92%).
columns.name: STP Rate %

columns.comment: Share of payments that needed a manual repair (fraction) = 1 - STP Rate.
columns.name: Repair Rate %

columns.comment: Number of payments that needed a manual repair - group by Repair Reason / Channel to see where they concentrate.
columns.name: Repairs

columns.comment: Average end-to-end processing time in hours (repaired payments take about half a day).
columns.name: Average Processing Hours

columns.comment: Share of payment value that is cross-border (fraction).
columns.name: Cross-Border Share %

columns.comment: Value of payments whose counterparty banks with a competitor (Other Bank), USD - wallet leakage.
columns.name: Volume via Other Banks USD

columns.comment: Share of payment value whose counterparty banks with a competitor (fraction). With Direction = Outbound and Payment Purpose = Supplier: how much of clients' supplier payments go to accounts at other banks.
columns.name: Share Paid via Other Banks %

columns.comment: Payment fee income in USD from the TB tariff: USD 3 per payment message plus 10 bps of cross-border value (a flow). Account-level TB fees (maintenance, channels, pooling) are in gold.fact_tb_fee_income_monthly.
columns.name: Fee Income USD

columns.comment: Distinct suppliers the selected clients paid through SMBC (outbound supplier payments, by pseudonymous counterparty id) - buyers paying >= 50 suppliers are SCF anchor candidates (dim_threshold SCF_ANCHOR_MIN_SUPPLIERS).
columns.name: Distinct Suppliers Paid

columns.comment: Legal entities (golden clients) with at least one payment in the selection.
columns.name: Paying Clients

comment: Client payments through SMBC APAC, Apr-2024 to Sep-2026 (USD): volume, count, average ticket, STP and repair rates, cross-border share, the share paid to accounts at other (competitor) banks, distinct suppliers paid and the tariff fee income, by channel (SWIFT MT, ISO 20022, host-to-host, payments API, portal, RTGS, FAST), direction, purpose (supplier, payroll, tax, intercompany, loan service, dividend, trade settlement), account currency, money corridor (payer->payee country) and counterparty bank. All measures are flows: they add up over any months. For "supplier payments to other banks" filter Direction = Outbound and Payment Purpose = Supplier. Grain: one row per payment message (gold.fact_payment_transaction).
